newsitem.title: INDIA: India carries out mock plane "hijacking".
newsitem.headline: India carries out mock plane "hijacking".

text.p: India staged a mock plane hijacking on Thursday that threw some senior officials into confusion until the government said it was only a drill to test security systems.
"It is a mock exercise. It was meant to test the systems," a government spokesman told Reuters.
Police and airline officials said Alliance Air flight 421A, carrying 29 passengers and six crew, was hijacked after it took off from New Delhi for the northern city of Jammu.
Alliance Air is a subsidiary of state-owned Indian Airlines.

Police in Jammu and Kashmir state initially said the Boeing 737, which left New Delhi at 3:15 p.m. (0945 GMT), had returned to the Indian capital after Pakistani authorities refused to allow it to land in the eastern city of Lahore.
Early reports about the mock hijacking confused even senior aviation officials, who said the plane had been hijacked over the northern state of Punjab near the border with Pakistan.
But authorities quickly denied the reports.

"There was a rumour that one Jammu-bound plane has been hijacked, but actually it was a mock exercise to get the response of the agencies involved in anti-hijacking operations," a Civil Aviation Ministry spokeswoman told Reuters.
"The response was found to be good."

Keen to make the drill look realistic, authorities posted a sign at the Alliance Air counter saying: "Alliance Air flight 421A has been hijacked. For further information, kindly contact our control room."
Less than an hour after takeoff, the plane turned around over Punjab and headed back to the capital.

"The message for the hijacking was given at 1605 hours (1035 GMT)," the Civil Aviation Ministry spokeswoman said. "The objective was to make it feel real, to check the effectiveness of the security systems."
At 4:30 p.m. (1100 GMT), the three "hijackers" demanded to speak to Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, the spokeswoman said. Thirty-five minutes later, the aircraft landed safely in Delhi.

Indian Airlines official Anoop Arora told Reuters that once on the ground, the mock hijackers released two passengers who had "fainted" and demanded that all vehicles be removed from around the aircraft, which was parked at a remote corner of the airport.

Alliance Air chief V. Kashyap told Reuters that the "hijackers" had been instructed to carry a gun and explosives, which they were to be allowed to take on board. "The whole thing was planned," he said.
Commandos, who Kashyap said were informed at the last minute that the operation was an exercise, stormed the plane, he said.
An hour and a half after the plane landed, security chiefs of Alliance Air and airport authorities were holding simulated negotiations with the "hijackers" in the airline terminal.
Kashyap said the pilot and the mock hijackers were the only people on board to know the operation was a drill.
"This allowed us to see how the crew, fire and ambulance workers, even commandos reacted," he said. "The last such test was 11 years ago. It was essential to see how we would react."
